verses.text: When Jesus had finished saying all this, He told His disciples,
“You know Passover is two days away. The Son of Man will be handed over to be crucified.”
Then the chief priests, legal experts, and elders gathered in the courtyard of the high priest, Caiaphas.
They plotted to seize Jesus by a trick and kill Him.
But they said, “Not during the festival, or the people might riot.”
Jesus was in Bethany at the house of Simon, who had been a leper.
A woman came with an alabaster jar of very costly perfume. While Jesus was eating, she poured it on His head.
When the disciples saw it, they got upset. “Why waste it like this?
That perfume could’ve sold for a lot and the money gone to the poor!”
Jesus knew what they were saying and replied, “Why are you giving this woman a hard time? She’s done something beautiful for Me.
The poor will always be with you, but I won’t always be here with you.
When she poured this perfume on My body, she was preparing Me for burial.
I’m telling you the truth: wherever this Good News is preached throughout the world, what she did will be told in her memory.”
Then one of the Twelve, Judas Iscariot, went to the chief priests
and asked, “What will you give me if I hand Him over to you?” They counted out thirty silver coins for him.
From then on, Judas looked for a chance to betray Jesus.
On the first day of Unleavened Bread, the disciples asked Jesus, “Where do You want us to prepare the Passover meal for You?”
He said, “Go into the city to a certain man and tell him, ‘The Teacher says, “My time is near. I’ll celebrate Passover at your house with My disciples.”’”
The disciples did what Jesus told them and got the Passover meal ready.
That evening, Jesus was reclining at the table with the Twelve.
While they were eating, He said, “I’m telling you the truth: one of you will betray Me.”
Deeply sad, each one began asking Him, “Surely it isn’t me, Lord?”
He answered, “The one who dipped his hand in the bowl with Me is the one who’ll betray Me.
The Son of Man is going as Scripture says, but how terrible for the one who betrays Him! It would’ve been better for that man if he’d never been born.”
Judas, the one who was betraying Him, asked, “Surely it isn’t me, Rabbi?” Jesus said, “You said it.”
While they were eating, Jesus took bread, gave thanks, broke it, and gave it to the disciples. “Take it and eat; this is My body.”
Then He took a cup, gave thanks, and passed it to them. “All of you, drink from it,
because this is My blood of the new covenant, poured out for many so their sins can be forgiven.
I’m telling you, I won’t drink this fruit of the vine again until that day I drink it new with you in My Father’s Kingdom.”
After they sang a hymn, they went out to the Mount of Olives.
Then Jesus told them, “Tonight you’ll all stumble because of Me. Scripture says, ‘I will strike the shepherd, and the flock’s sheep will scatter.’
But after I’m raised, I’ll go ahead of you to Galilee.”
Peter answered, “Even if everyone else stumbles because of You, I never will.”
Jesus told him, “I’m telling you the truth: tonight, before the rooster crows, you’ll deny knowing Me three times.”
Peter said, “Even if I have to die with You, I will never deny You.” All the other disciples said the same.
Then Jesus went with them to a place called Gethsemane. He told His disciples, “Sit here while I go over there and pray.”
He took Peter and the two sons of Zebedee with Him. He began to feel deep sorrow and anguish.
Then He told them, “My soul is overwhelmed with sorrow, even to the point of death. Stay here and keep watch with Me.”
He went a little farther, fell face down, and prayed, “My Father, if it’s possible, let this cup pass from Me. Still, let it be what You want, not what I want.”
He came back to the disciples and found them sleeping. He said to Peter, “Couldn’t you stay awake with Me for even one hour?
Stay alert and pray so you don’t fall into temptation. The spirit is willing, but the body is weak.”
A second time He went away and prayed, “My Father, if this cup can’t pass unless I drink it, let Your will be done.”
He came back and found them asleep again; their eyes were so heavy.
He left them, went away again, and prayed a third time, saying the same thing.
Then He returned to the disciples and said, “You’re still sleeping and resting? Look, the hour is near. The Son of Man is being handed over to sinners.
Get up, let’s go. Look, the one betraying Me is here.”
While He was still speaking, Judas, one of the Twelve, arrived with a large crowd carrying swords and clubs, sent by the chief priests and elders.
The betrayer had arranged a signal: “The man I kiss is the one. Grab Him.”
Right away Judas came to Jesus and said, “Greetings, Rabbi!” Then he kissed Him.
Jesus said to him, “Friend, why are you here?” Then the crowd grabbed Jesus and arrested Him.
One of Jesus’ companions reached for his sword, drew it, and struck the high priest’s servant, cutting off his ear.
Jesus told him, “Put your sword back where it belongs. Everyone who uses the sword will die by the sword.
Do you think I can’t ask My Father, and He’d send more than twelve legions of angels right now?
But then how would the Scriptures come true, that this has to happen?”
At that moment Jesus said to the crowd, “Did you come out to arrest Me like I’m a robber, with swords and clubs? I sat in the temple teaching every day, and you didn’t arrest Me.
But all this has happened to fulfill what the prophets wrote.” Then all the disciples left Him and ran away.
The people who arrested Jesus took Him to Caiaphas the high priest, where the legal experts and elders had gathered.
Peter followed from a distance to the high priest’s courtyard. He went in and sat with the guards to see how it would end.
The chief priests, elders, and whole council looked for false testimony against Jesus so they could put Him to death.
They couldn’t find any, even though many false witnesses came forward. Finally two came forward
and said, “This man said, ‘I can tear down God’s temple and rebuild it in three days.’”
The high priest stood up and asked Him, “Aren’t You going to answer? What do You say about these accusations?”
But Jesus stayed silent. The high priest said to Him, “I put You under oath by the living God: tell us if You are the Christ, God’s Son.”
Jesus answered, “You’ve said it. But I tell you this: from now on you’ll see the Son of Man seated at the right hand of Power and coming on heaven’s clouds.”
Then the high priest tore his clothes and said, “He has blasphemed! Why do we need more witnesses? You heard the blasphemy yourselves.
What’s your verdict?” They answered, “He deserves death!”
Then they spat in His face and punched Him. Others slapped Him,
saying, “Come on, Christ, prophesy to us! Who hit You?”
Peter was sitting outside in the courtyard. A servant girl came up and said, “You were with Jesus the Galilean too!”
But he denied it in front of everyone: “I don’t know what you’re talking about.”
When he went out to the entrance, another person saw him and told the people there, “This man was with Jesus of Nazareth too.”
Again Peter denied it, swearing, “I don’t know the man!”
A little later, the people standing there came over to Peter. “You’re definitely one of them; your accent gives you away.”
Then Peter began cursing and swearing, “I don’t know the man!” At once, a rooster crowed.
Peter remembered what Jesus had told him: “Before the rooster crows, you’ll deny Me three times.” He went outside and wept bitterly.
